mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, the 20-day S&P 500 return is negative in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, the 5-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and housing starts (HOUST < 1500) indicates a contraction in the real economy, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 100 and HOUST is below 1500, the 20-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 annualized growth > 3.0%), a decline in consumer spending (RSAFS < 360000) signals an impending slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 annualized growth exceeds 3.0% and RSAFS is below 360000, the 20-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST > 1500) indicates strong consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 1500, the 60-day S&P 500 return is negative in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A high inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized) signals potential monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, the 20-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS > 137000) and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals an overheating economy followed by aggressive monetary tightening, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS exceeds 137000 and FEDFUNDS is above 5.0%, the 5-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO < 100), a decline in industrial production signals reduced output capacity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 100, the 60-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of instances.
